Shares of SK Hynix were trading down 4.9%, compared with 2.2% decline in the benchmark KOSPI (.KS11) as of 0036 GMT.

item.title: Bessent's D-Day sanctions are more Anzio, but Iran response is key
item.description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent invoked the famous D-Day landing of Allied troops in France in 1944 when announcing new sanctions against Iran.
item.dc:creator: Clyde Russell
item.content:encoded: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent invoked the famous D-Day landing of Allied troops in France in 1944 when announcing new sanctions against Iran. But the measures are better compared to another World War Two amphibious landing, the considerably less successful Anzio beachhead in Italy. The Anzio battle was marked by the initial success of Allied landings, but a lack of decisive leadership saw the campaign stall and turn into a months-long campaign of attrition that largely failed to achieve its initial objectives. Bessent's new [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"measures"] aim to strangle Iran economically and target countries and corporates doing business with the Islamic Republic in five sectors, namely digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping. But rather than going for broke up front, Bessent is putting countries on notice that they will have to work with the United States or face losing access to the global dollar-based financial system. In other words, the new measures are more of a threat than a reality. But even if they do become reality there are doubts as to whether they will be effective enough to force Iran's rulers to capitulate, or indeed whether they will be severe enough to force a desperate Iranian populace to successfully rise up and overthrow their clerical rulers. Iran has proven adept at getting around sanctions in the past by setting up new front companies and working with its allies such as China. With Beijing unlikely to join any U.S. sanctions, it would mean that Bessent would have to be willing to impose measures against Chinese banks, refiners, shippers and traders, a level of escalation that Washington may be cautious about pursuing. What the new sanctions do achieve is to confirm that a diplomatic solution to the Iran conflict is a distant option, and they reinforce the view being put forward by the administration of President Donald Trump that some form of victory is still possible. Another lesson from history is that when both sides in a war are convinced they can still win and that time is on their side, the conflict will continue until this calculation shifts. IRANIAN RESPONSE The key for energy markets will be how Iran responds. The messaging so far on social media has been belligerent, but Iran has also yet to renew missile and drone attacks on energy and other infrastructure in Gulf nations hosting U.S. bases, such as Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain. Tehran has also not been able to fully close the Strait of Hormuz, and while there is some [USN:L1N44L00N TEXT:"dispute"] over the actual volume of crude moving through the narrow waterway, the key point is it's not zero and every barrel that gets through lessens Iran's leverage. Iran is also feeling pain from the existing U.S. blockade of its ports, a measure that is proving far more effective than financial sanctions. Iran exported an average of 1.75 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude in the three months leading up to the U.S. and Israeli attacks on February 28, according to data compiled by commodity analysts Kpler. This has plunged to just 255,000 bpd in August, down from 893,000 bpd in July and even weaker than the 259,000 bpd from May, which was the lowest since May 2020, a period when crude demand was hit by the COVID-19 pandemic. The problem for Bessent and Trump is that the more their blockade and economic sanctions work, the more they incentivise Iran to hit back with every military means at its disposal. If Iran's leaders see themselves in an existential battle, they are unlikely to meekly accept being economically throttled without attempting to wrest back the initiative through hitting infrastructure and vessels across the Gulf. The uncertainty of Iran's response is likely to keep a nervous premium in crude oil prices. Global benchmark Brent futures did ease after Bessent's announcement, falling around 2.4% on Monday to $92.17 a barrel. But this is still 31% higher than the $70.14 a barrel they dropped to during the brief ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran, which lasted from mid-June to early July. Enjoying this column? item.title: Premiê britânico diz que Reino Unido deve ser “mais ousado” na busca por laços com a UE
item.description: O primeiro-ministro britânico, Andy Burnham, disse ao presidente do Conselho Europeu, António Costa, que Londres deve ser mais ousada na busca por laços mais estreitos com a União Europeia, e que a cúpula entre o Reino Unido e a UE prevista para este ano oferece essa oportunidade, informou seu gabinete nesta segunda-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O primeiro-ministro britânico, Andy Burnham, disse ao presidente do Conselho Europeu, António Costa, que Londres deve ser mais ousada na busca por laços mais estreitos com a União Europeia, e que a cúpula entre o Reino Unido e a UE prevista para este ano oferece essa oportunidade, informou seu gabinete nesta segunda-feira. Burnham se reuniu com Costa no final do domingo, durante viagem a Kiev para copresidir uma reunião da chamada “Coalizão dos Dispostos”, em sua primeira visita à Ucrânia desde que assumiu o cargo de primeiro-ministro. Segundo seu gabinete, Burnham disse a Costa que o Reino Unido deveria aproveitar a cooperação existente em defesa e segurança com os aliados europeus e buscar uma colaboração mais estreita em todas as esferas do relacionamento. O líder britânico disse a Costa que o Reino Unido “precisa ser mais ousado no sentido de se aproximar do bloco”, afirmou uma porta-voz de Downing Street sobre as conversas entre os dois líderes. “Isso inclui aproveitar os laços estreitos de defesa e segurança já estabelecidos entre o Reino Unido e os aliados europeus para promover uma maior cooperação em todas as áreas do relacionamento.”

item.title: Orçamento de 2027 está encaminhado e salário mínimo será de R$1.741, diz Durigan

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que o projeto da Lei Orçamentária Anual (PLOA) de 2027 está bem encaminhado dentro do governo e que já foi definido o valor do salário mínimo em R$1.741 para o ano que vem, valor resultante de reajustes previstos na legislação. Durigan, que fez questão de destacar que está mantida a indexação de outros benefícios ao salário mínimo, esteve reunido mais cedo com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e a ministra da Casa Civil, Miriam Belchior. "O salário mínimo, com os reajustes previstos em lei, chega a R$1.741 no ano que vem e ele, necessariamente cumprindo a legislação brasileira, dentro do nosso espírito de privilegiar a população mais carente, vai também para a Previdência, vai também para os benefícios que têm a indexação com o salário mínimo", disse o ministro a jornalistas. "O Orçamento está muito bem encaminhado, com o salário mínimo definido", acrescentou. O salário mínimo é reajustado anualmente levando-se em conta a inflação do período e a variação do PIB de dois anos antes, mas a valorização é sujeita a limitações do arcabouço fiscal. Segundo Durigan, o PLOA deve já prever o novo modelo da reforma tributária. O Executivo federal tem, segundo regras constitucionais, até o dia 31 de agosto para encaminhar ao Congresso seu projeto de lei orçamentária para o ano seguinte. O Congresso, por sua vez, tem até 22 de dezembro, em tese, para devolver o projeto -- já votado -- para sanção presidencial.

item.title: Seul diz que Coreia do Sul e EUA se comprometem a manter cooperação estreita em relação à Coreia do Norte
item.description: O ministro das Relações Exteriores da Coreia do Sul, Cho Hyun, e o secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, conversaram nesta segunda-feira, e o governo sul-coreano informou que ambos concordaram em manter uma comunicação e cooperação estreitas para resolver a questão nuclear norte-coreana, segundo noticiou a agência de notícias sul-coreana Yonhap.
item.dc:creator: David Brunnstrom
item.content:encoded: O ministro das Relações Exteriores da Coreia do Sul, Cho Hyun, e o secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, conversaram nesta segunda-feira, e o governo sul-coreano informou que ambos concordaram em manter uma comunicação e cooperação estreitas para resolver a questão nuclear norte-coreana, segundo noticiou a agência de notícias sul-coreana Yonhap. O Departamento de Estado dos EUA divulgou apenas uma breve declaração sobre a conversa telefônica, que ocorre em um momento de tensão entre os aliados. O presidente Donald Trump anunciou recentemente uma redução nos exercícios militares conjuntos e elogiou a Coreia do Norte, que possui armas nucleares, ao mesmo tempo em que afirmou que Seul não havia ajudado em seus esforços para tentar desnuclearizar o Irã. O Departamento de Estado informou que Rubio e Cho discutiram “uma série de questões relacionadas à Aliança EUA-ROK”, referindo-se à Coreia do Sul pelas iniciais em inglês de seu nome oficial, República da Coreia. “O secretário destacou a necessidade de os dois países permanecerem em estreita coordenação em assuntos que são essenciais para a aliança”, acrescentou. A Yonhap informou que, em um comunicado sobre as conversas, o Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Coreia do Sul não mencionou se os diplomatas reafirmaram seu compromisso habitual com a desnuclearização da Coreia do Norte, apesar de terem enfatizado a importância da cooperação na questão nuclear norte-coreana. “O ministro e o secretário concordaram em manter uma comunicação e cooperação estreitas entre a Coreia do Sul e os EUA em prol da paz na Península Coreana e da resolução da questão nuclear norte-coreana, ao mesmo tempo em que mantêm uma postura sólida de defesa conjunta”, informou a Yonhap, citando o comunicado do ministério. A agência citou Cho afirmando que Seul faria o possível para ajudar a garantir que a recente mensagem de Trump à Coreia do Norte levasse à retomada do diálogo entre Washington e Pyongyang e à paz na península. ABERTURA DE TRUMP TESTA ALIANÇA O gesto de paz de Trump a Kim Jong Un, da Coreia do Norte, na semana passada, aliado às suas críticas a Seul, gerou preocupação entre analistas de que a imprevisibilidade de Trump possa prejudicar as alianças que há muito mantêm a paz na Ásia. Cho afirmou na semana passada que a ordem de Trump para reduzir os exercícios militares parecia ter como objetivo, em parte, pressionar Seul a apoiar os esforços dos EUA na guerra contra o Irã, além de outras questões ainda não resolvidas, como investimentos. Ele disse que uma possível fonte de atrito poderia ser o compromisso da Coreia do Sul de investir US$350 bilhões nos Estados Unidos, no âmbito de um acordo comercial assinado no ano passado. Seul ainda não anunciou detalhes do plano de investimento, embora Cho tenha dito que Washington tinha enviado a Seul uma proposta delineando projetos que poderiam ser considerados. A Yonhap citou o comunicado do ministério, segundo o qual os dois lados concordaram em trabalhar em prol de resultados “mutuamente benéficos” em várias questões pendentes, incluindo tarifas, investimentos e cooperação em segurança. A agência informou que Cho ressaltou o compromisso do governo de Seul em fazer contribuições substanciais para ajudar a restaurar a livre passagem pelo Estreito de Ormuz, ao mesmo tempo em que destacou a liderança ativa de Trump e dos EUA na abordagem da questão do Oriente Médio. A agência informou que Cho e Rubio concordaram em se reunir em breve para discutir em profundidade as principais questões pendentes.

item.title: Tiger Woods set for first in-person court appearance on DUI charge
item.description: After several postponements, Tiger Woods is scheduled to appear before a judge in person for the first time since his car accident on March 27.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: After several postponements, Tiger Woods is scheduled to appear before a judge in person for the first time since his car accident on March 27. Woods will appear in court at 8:30 a.m. ET on Tuesday, Sept. 8, in Martin County, Fla., according to multiple reports that cited county records. He faces two misdemeanor charges of DUI with property damage and refusal to submit to a lawful test. Woods, 50, has pleaded not guilty. Police who responded to the crash in Jupiter Island, Fla., found two hydrocodone pills in Woods' pocket and observed signs of impairment. A breathalyzer test found he did not have alcohol in his system, but he refused a urine test. Prosecutors have extended the investigative process as they sought and eventually were granted access to Woods' hospital records the day of the crash. Woods' court date was postponed multiple times amid the process. He also spent time in Zurich, Switzerland, seeking specialized treatment after the two-car accident. Douglas Duncan, Woods' attorney, seeks a jury trial. --Field Level Media

item.title: Former Mercer standout Braden Atkinson wins Oregon State QB job
item.description: Former FCS star Braden Atkinson beat out incumbent Maalik Murphy and fellow transfer Brady Jones to earn the Oregon State starting quarterback gig.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former FCS star Braden Atkinson beat out incumbent Maalik Murphy and fellow transfer Brady Jones to earn the Oregon State starting quarterback gig. The Beavers named Atkinson the starter on Monday after a lengthy, spirited competition between the three players. Atkinson played last season at Mercer and won the Jerry Rice Award as the top freshman player in FCS. He completed 66% of his passes and set single-season school records of 3,596 yards and 34 touchdown passes. Atkinson, who tossed 11 interceptions, also set a Mercer single-game record with 533 passing yards against VMI on Oct. 25. He finished fifth in balloting for the Walter Payton Award, the honor that goes to the top FCS offensive player. Murphy completed 58.1% of his throws for 1,805 yards, nine touchdowns and eight interceptions last season for Oregon State, which went 2-8 in his 10 appearances. Murphy played at Texas and Duke before relocating to the Pacific Northwest. In 2024, he passed for 2,933 yards and 26 touchdowns and was picked off 12 times as the Blue Devils' starter. He redshirted at Texas in 2022 and started two of seven games played in 2023 when he passed for 477 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. Overall, he has passed for 5,215 yards and 38 touchdowns against 23 interceptions as a collegian. Jones, a Murrieta, Calif., native, was 19-of-40 passing for 136 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions in limited action as a junior for Western Michigan last season. Former Alabama co-offensive coordinator JaMarcus Shephard is the new head coach at Oregon State, which is part of a reconfigured Pac-12. The Beavers open the season Sept. 5 with a nonconference game at No. 23 Houston. --Field Level Media

item.title: LSU's Lane Kiffin defends adding NFL players who want 5th NCAA season
item.description: LSU is poised to become the first FBS program to sign undrafted free agents released by NFL teams, but coach Lane Kiffin defended his pursuit of such players, saying "most" coaches will soon be recruiting from the same pool.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: LSU is poised to become the first FBS program to sign undrafted free agents released by NFL teams, but coach Lane Kiffin defended his pursuit of such players, saying "most" coaches will soon be recruiting from the same pool. Tight end Dae'Quan Wright, who played for Kiffin at Ole Miss over the past two seasons, plans to join LSU once he clears NFL waivers, according to his agents Sunday. Wright was most recently with the Cleveland Browns, but he did not play in their most recent preseason game and was officially waived Monday. Another domino fell Monday when former Ole Miss defensive lineman Zxavian Harris, who was waived by the New Orleans Saints, revealed on his Instagram that he intends to join Kiffin at LSU, labeling it a "business decision." Wright, Harris and 14 other players have only one additional year of NCAA eligibility thanks to a Louisiana court that granted them a temporary restraining order last week, allowing them to enter the transfer portal to keep their options open. The order is related to the NCAA's new age-based eligibility model, which allows five seasons within a five-year window and did not cover players from the high school Class of 2022 who had already exhausted their eligibility. "In my opinion, knowing the information, I think it's really wrong to be critical of these kids," Kiffin said at a press conference Monday. "They were granted a fifth year by a judge saying that they were wronged by the NCAA and that they should've had the fifth year all along like all the kids moving forward will have a fifth year." Ex-Notre Dame defensive end Junior Tuihalamaka, another plaintiff in the case, committed to the Tigers last Friday, though he had no NFL ties like Wright and Harris. "At the end of the day, because of these rulings, they're either going to play for you or they're going to play for someone else around the country," Kiffin said. "So we've made the decision to recruit them like probably most people are." Kiffin drew criticism last winter for his exit from Ole Miss to take the helm of an SEC rival while the Rebels were still in the College Football Playoff. Several of his assistant coaches followed him to LSU, but he allowed offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. and others to return to Ole Miss to coach in the playoff. The co-founder and executive director of the Grove Collective, Ole Miss' NIL machine, even claimed during a Monday podcast appearance that the FBI searched for "bugs" in the football offices after Kiffin left. "We knew kind of what was in Baton Rouge, and we knew how they operated. I remember getting on my knees and looking underneath the desk, like checking for, ‘Is there some sort of bug in my office?'" Walker Jones told the "Assorted Crackers" podcast, later insisting, "Trust me, you don't know this guy (Kiffin) like I do." Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed to ESPN on Monday that an FBI agent walked through the Rebels' offices to aid a search. He was not a direct hire by the university in this matter, but rather the father of an Ole Miss player. Kiffin ultimately had four players follow him from Oxford to Baton Rouge: defensive end Princewill Umanmielen, linebacker TJ Dottery, receiver Winston Watkins Jr. and offensive tackle Devin Harper. And with the season opener against Clemson less than two weeks away, Kiffin apparently is not done adding players to his new program. "I believe that my job is to LSU and the LSU people that hired me and the fans," Kiffin said. --Field Level Media

item.title: Judge rejects First Brands' plan to pay down debts by pursuing lawsuits
item.description: A U.S. bankruptcy judge on Monday rejected auto parts maker First Brands' proposal to pay back creditors by pursuing litigation against insiders, instead converting the case to a more straightforward Chapter 7 liquidation.
item.dc:creator: Dietrich Knauth
item.content:encoded: A U.S. bankruptcy judge on Monday rejected auto parts maker First Brands' proposal to pay back creditors by pursuing litigation against insiders, instead converting the case to a more straightforward Chapter 7 liquidation. U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Christopher Lopez said that First Brands' proposed Chapter 11 plan was not acceptable, in part because it sought to defer payment on at least $222 million in debts racked up during the company's bankruptcy. First Brands owes billions more from before its bankruptcy, and its efforts to sell off business lines generated only a fraction of what it owes to its creditors. “Unfortunately, time was not on the debtor's side,” Lopez said. “The sales process did not render the types of sales prices I'm sure everybody wanted.” First Brands' collapse caused losses for some of the largest investment firms on Wall Street and sparked concerns about fund managers' exposure to troubled borrowers in the opaque markets for private credit. The company's preferred liquidation plan would have set up litigation trusts to help pursue lawsuits in hopes of raising additional money for creditors over time. But under First Brands’ proposal, the lawsuits would need to bring in $1.9 billion before the company could fully repay the administrative claims that must be paid first, Lopez said. Creditors who opposed the bankruptcy plan, as well as the U.S. Justice Department’s bankruptcy watchdog, expressed doubt that the company's [USN:L6N3WG0C6 TEXT:"litigation"] would result in a meaningful recovery from people like the company's indicted founder, Patrick James. James and his brother Edward James were indicted on fraud charges in January, and they have pleaded [USN:L6N3Z0184 TEXT:"not guilty"]. First Brands did not immediately respond to a request for comment. First Brands filed for bankruptcy in September with about $14 million in cash and more than $9 billion in liabilities. The company borrowed an additional $1.1 billion from its existing group of lenders early in its bankruptcy but [USN:L6N3ZN122 TEXT:"burned through"] most of that cash by January, forcing it to rely on prepayments from key parts buyers like Ford (F.N) and GM (GM.N) . First Brands sought to find a buyer for the whole company but was able to sell only a few business lines to generate a fraction of the amount it borrowed under the bankruptcy loan. It sold its Horizon towing business for $64 million, its Toledo Molding & Die business for $80 million and its Walbro business for $50 million.
